decided: The closing commit is offered only when staging would actually change something: a new file, or a tracked file that differs from the last commit. When the only changes cancel out, no commit is offered, and a push still owed is still offered.
alternatives: offer the commit whenever git lists any change, and let the user recover from the failed empty commit
why: Offering a commit that fails with nothing to commit would also block the push behind it. One extra read-only comparison with the last commit avoids that; a rare case where a file was untracked and left unchanged on disk stays a named limit.
